message: No rust-contract artifact exists for clarity-web/src/intent/types/ or for behavior.rs. All 14 obligations (REQ-BH-1..REQ-BH-14) have clause_origin=INFERRED and requires_contract=true. The plan §2 openly discloses this gap; §9 marks it BLOCKING for proof-writer. The requires_contract flag is an indicator, not a schema-level enforcement gate (no blocked_by_contract or gate field exists in proof-obligation/v1). proof-writer reads obligations by status=planned and would not pause on the flag. Without a ratified contract, proof-writer risks writing specs against clauses that rust-contract may later correct or reject.
required_fix: rust-contract must author contract.md (or equivalent) for clarity-web/src/intent/types/ with explicit clauses keyed to the 14 requirement IDs. Each clause must carry a clause_origin=AUTHORED tag and either ratify or correct the inferred text in plan §3. Three open algebraic decisions in §3 (MAX_* contract status, with_verification semantics, &mut Self builder signature) must be resolved as part of ratification.
blocker_reason: Schema requires contract_clause to be authored; 14 of 14 obligations have INFERRED clauses. Proof-writer cannot proceed with material uncertainty on every clause.

message: Every one of the 21 obligation rows is missing 8 schema-required fields per proof-obligation/v1: schema_version, domain_claim, risk_tags, workdir, model_bounds, tool_metadata, trusted_base_refs, behavior_affecting. The rows as planned will not validate against the published schema. Total missing-field occurrences: 8 fields × 21 rows = 168.
required_fix: Regenerate proofs/behavior-obligations.planned.jsonl with all required fields populated. For each row: schema_version=proof-obligation/v1, domain_claim (a one-line high-level claim distinct from contract_clause), risk_tags (array, e.g., ["boundary","serde","refinement"]), workdir (always /home/lewis/src/clarity), model_bounds (object with concrete bounds or empty {}), tool_metadata (object with verus_version, proptest_version), trusted_base_refs (array referencing trusted-base-ledger/v1 rows), behavior_affecting (true/false per obligation — most V obligations are behavior_affecting=true).
blocker_reason: Rows cannot be parsed as proof-obligation/v1. Downstream formal-verifier will reject the ledger entry for these rows.

message: PO-P1 proptest strategy uses string_regex("[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,30}") for snake_case names but does not pin an invariant that is_valid_behavior_name(&name) holds for every generated name. Without this, the strategy could drift from the source classifier (e.g., a future regex edit that allows 'A...' uppercase) and the round-trip property would silently weaken. This is a vacuity risk for the L7 property's value.
required_fix: Proof-writer must add to the arb_behavior() strategy: after generating the name, assert is_valid_behavior_name(&name) holds. This binds the generated name distribution to the source predicate, preventing strategy drift.
approval_ref: proof-writer must update PO-P1 strategy before execution
rationale: Non-behavior-affecting strengthening of an already-accepted obligation; can be added during proof-writer pass without re-running the plan review.

message: PO-P1 strategy says 'optional Verification' but does not specify a sub-strategy. The default proptest behavior on an Option<T> is to generate None ~50% of the time and use the default Some(T) the other 50%, which would never exercise non-default Verification field values. Verification has 3 String fields (verification_type, description, example) all of which are interesting to round-trip.
required_fix: Proof-writer must define arb_verification() = (string_regex('[a-z_]{1,20}'), '.*', '.*') and use prop::option::of(arb_verification()) in the Behavior strategy. This ensures Some(Verification) is exercised with non-default values.
approval_ref: proof-writer must update PO-P1 strategy before execution

message: §6 enumerates 7 trust anchors (serde_json round-trip, Vec::push order-preservation, String totality, Err-arm shape, MAX_* literals, struct closure) but does not commit to producing trusted-base-ledger/v1 rows. PO-P1 will need #[verifier::external_body] on serde_json calls (plan §8 mentions this in prose), which generates trust markers, which need ledger entries. Per proof-schemas.md every assume / axiom / external_body / trusted marker needs a row.
required_fix: Proof-writer must produce trusted-base-ledger.jsonl alongside Verus specs. One row per trust anchor in plan §6, plus rows for each #[verifier::external_body] marker added during write (expected: 2 rows for serde_json::to_string and serde_json::from_str in PO-P1). Each row must include trusted_kind, reason, scope, compensating_evidence, owner, reviewer_disposition.
approval_ref: proof-writer must produce trusted-base-ledger.jsonl with PO-P1 specs
rationale: Schema compliance gap; non-behavior-affecting; can be added in write phase.

message: PO-V9 assumption cites 'order of update-struct-expression evaluation is left-to-right'. Rust does not specify evaluation order of struct literal fields; the ..self syntax copies remaining fields after explicit ones, so the result is order-independent. The law (commutativity of with_description × with_verification) holds regardless, but the cited mechanism is imprecise. Verus spec should be a structural postcondition comparing the two result structs field-by-field, not a timing argument.
required_fix: Proof-writer: rewrite PO-V9 ensures clause as a field-by-field extensional equality (5 conjuncts) rather than relying on evaluation-order semantics.
approval_ref: Will be addressed in proof-writer spec
rationale: Spec imprecision, not unsoundness. Law holds; only the cited reasoning needs sharpening.

message: add_precondition's fluent &mut Self -> &mut Self return is in the public signature (line 86) but is not exercised within this module's tests (lines 211-214, 225-228 push directly to the Vec, bypassing the builder). REQ-BH-11's order-preservation law depends on the fluent signature but is somewhat hypothetical within this module. The plan §8 commits to a new test_add_precondition_order test that chains .add_precondition(...).add_precondition(...) — this is correct and resolves the gap.
required_fix: Proof-writer: ensure the new test_add_precondition_order test in the bridge (PO-V11) actually chains two calls via the fluent return, asserting the preconditions == [x, y] result. The plan already commits to this in §8.
approval_ref: Will be addressed in proof-writer test additions
rationale: Test coverage gap inside the existing test module; plan already commits to fix in §8.

message: feature.rs::validate (line 85-101) and spec.rs::validate (line 112-151) do NOT call behavior.validate() per-element. A Behavior with 21 preconditions embedded in a Feature/Spec will pass the parent's validate() with Ok(()). This is a real validator-composition gap but is out of scope for behavior.rs's proof plan. The plan correctly scopes to Behavior's own surface.
required_fix: Out of scope for cl-ooz. Flag for feature.rs (cl-...) and spec.rs (cl-...) proof plans. Each parent's validate() should either (a) iterate self.behaviors / self.features[*].behaviors and call b.validate() transitively, or (b) explicitly document why composition is the caller's responsibility. Either resolution is a future-proofing concern, not a cl-ooz defect.
rationale: Cross-module observation; not behavior.rs's responsibility to prove composition.

message: Workspace has no verifier-lane-decisions.jsonl. The obligations JSONL conflates lane decisions (verifier, applicability, decision_reason, non_applicability_evidence_refs) with proof obligations (target, command, artifact, expected_evidence). Per proof-schemas.md, these are distinct schemas: verifier-lane-decision/v1 and proof-obligation/v1. The reviewer can reconstruct the lane decisions from the obligations rows (each row carries a verifier field) and produces verifier-lane-review.jsonl (this file). But the upstream verifier-lane-decisions.jsonl is missing as a planner artifact.
required_fix: For this cl-ooz review, the reviewer accepts the folded obligations JSONL and produces verifier-lane-review.jsonl. For future plans, the planner should produce both files: a separate verifier-lane-decisions.jsonl (one row per (requirement_id, contract_clause, proof_seed_id, verifier) tuple with applicability/decision_reason/non_applicability_evidence_refs/limitation_kind fields) and a separate proof-obligations.planned.jsonl (one row per obligation with target/command/artifact/expected_evidence fields).
approval_ref: verifier-lane-review.jsonl produced with 21 rows; see proofs/verifier-lane-review.jsonl
rationale: Reviewer compensated for missing planner artifact by producing the lane-review output directly.
